title: Moderate prenatal alcohol exposure differentially alters acute ethanol sensitivity of GABAergic transmission in CRFR1- and CRFR1+ CeM Neurons.
ehr_evidence: Male CRF1-Cre transgenic rats were obtained for breeding from Dr. Nicholas Gilpin, Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center (New Orleans, LA, USA).
summary: Experimental study investigating how moderate prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) on gestational day 12 alters acute ethanol modulation of GABAergic neurotransmission onto CRFR1+ and CRFR1- neurons in the central amygdala of adult rat offspring.
key_findings: PAE increased basal sIPSC amplitude in CRFR1+ neurons (F(1, 127) = 5.026, p = 0.027).
In air males, 66 mM EtOH decreased CRFR1- sIPSC frequency (t(11) = 2.658, p = 0.022), but PAE males showed no significant change at 44 mM (p = 0.279), 66 mM (p = 0.138), or 88 mM (p = 0.484).
PAE males exhibited a significant decrease in CRFR1+ sIPSC frequency at 44 mM EtOH (t(8) = 2.465, p = 0.039).
PAE females showed significant decreases in CRFR1- sIPSC frequency at 44 mM (t(11) = 3.805, p = 0.003) and 66 mM (t(9) = 2.775, p = 0.022) EtOH.
PAE females exhibited significant decreases in CRFR1+ sIPSC frequency (t(8) = 3.196, p = 0.013) and amplitude (t(9) = 2.719, p = 0.023) at 44 mM EtOH.
population: Adult CRF1-Cre transgenic rat offspring (P80-110), both males and females
exposure_domain: Prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) and acute ethanol
limitations: Use of transgenic reporter lines may alter neurophysiology via insertional mutagenesis or promoter leakiness.
Recordings performed at room temperature rather than physiologically relevant temperature.
Potential incongruence between reporter gene expression and endogenous CRFR1 expression.
Small sample sizes per experimental group (n=9-12 cells/animals).
